comments.author: @Crates-Media
comments.text:
Regarding the argument that UBI is a slippery slope towards dystopia, that seems like a rather myopic stance on what is essentially a form of socialism. To me, that's akin to saying, "If the government goes and opens up public locations where they buy the most popular books and reference materials at the cost of taxpayers, that means they can control which books people will be allowed to read. They can decide which people to allow inside the building, or to whom they will lend books. They can use your social credit score to decide how many days you get to keep the book. They can raise the fines for not returning a book to help pay for their mismanaged resources and lazy staff."

Obviously, I'm talking about public libraries. In reality, none of those things have happened after over two centuries of the government supplying free books, maps, magazines, videos and even video games to the public at essentially no transactional cost (as the cost is paid from our taxes). When there is a strong incentive to offer something that everyone truly needs and can derive great value from, this proves that it can be offered without turning into a dystopian nightmare. When I hear people saying, "How dare the average taxpayer bear the burden of university education when there are rich kids getting those subsidies?" it's immediately clear that the person saying it has no concept that there are indeed many privileged families with kids in public schools and using public libraries. It's socialism! Hide your kids and hide your wife!

comments.author: @Jackson_Zheng
comments.text:
I don't get why people think AI agent run businesses is such a bad idea. Like, inherently they'd have no use for the extra money and resources they acquire, except for growing their infrastructure. However, if this was capped and artificial boundaries were put into place just like how antitrust laws, then we wouldn't have to worry as much about it getting out of control. All the money they make can be funneled into a non-profit or distributed at mass as a form of UBI. 
Since AI run businesses would be extremely lean and efficient (much more so than humans), they'd be able to make almost everything a commodity, driving the cost of products down to the raw material costs. Food and water would be free, and so would travel and eventually transportation once AI starts to operate manufacturing plants. There would be no laws being broken, no ethical issues within the company (since all the employees are just AI as well).

If this was to happen, eventually, AI would almost become synonymous with mother nature. Just like how humans don't have to evaporate large parts of the ocean to make clouds so it can rain to produce drinkable water since that's mother nature's job, AI would take over production of the bare necessities like food, water transportation and energy.
As for the rest of us humans, we'd still have our own economy, selling and exchanging whatever we find valuable with each other - that's not gonna go away. "What" we find valuable will change, but the fact that we will always want better, nicer and more extravagant and luxurious stuff - that part of human nature is never gonna change.

As for arguments against UBI, like how people will just become lazy and do nothing all day, most people don't fully understand the scope of what UBI provides. All that UBI would provide is a way to meet the most basic of human needs without having to actively spend time to maintain survival. It's not gonna make everyone rich, it's just gonna raise the standard of living for people at the bottom of the social class. The rich wouldn't give a shit, the extra money would be meaningless to them since they earn so much anyway. So what would this look like?
Well, imagine going back to your childhood days, but now, there's no parents telling you what to do, there's no "school" that you'll have to mandatory attend, and you don't have to think about bills or food or anything like that. Now extend that experience to the rest of your life - that is basically what UBI would provide. Sure, if you wanted to do nothing and watch movies all day, you can. But someone has to make those movies and eventually, you'll probably get bored of them and hedonic adaptation will kick in, forcing you to do something more productive to ease that boredom.

comments.text:
The eventuality of UBI is probably one of the most immediate doomsday scenarios for AI. 

I found the poll interesting, but the audience is most likely very skewed in favor of AI (I’m not an AI alarmist, I’ve got a several decades long tech background) and most likely leans very Left on the whole. 

I would mention that (a) UBI has been tried and is currently being tried in the US and it’s NOT working overall, and (b) what on God’s green earth in the history of the US gives you any basis for expecting anything other than disaster?  When has any large group received ongoing cash from the govt and come out better on the other side?  

And, based on recent events, what makes you believe that this won’t be used to create an authoritarian state?  

Do you really believe our state and federal governments will suddenly become benign and even benevolent groups in service of all citizens? How does that happen?

So, if UBI is the only plausible solution to this challenge that AI will pose, and if UBI is certain to fail (okay, my opinion), then do we just march forward anyway, saying “what else can we do?”
